text: Match night and the whole city ordered in - my fries took two hours and arrived cold as the losing team's batting.
Festival-eve order: sent someone else's paneer sandwich instead of my pasta, 80 minutes late. Support blamed the rush.
Pre-match crowd everywhere, one cappuccino took 22 minutes while staff shouted ticket numbers over each other.
Cafe packed with match-watchers glued to phones for hours. Four of us stood at the door, not one table freed up.
Match dekhne wale sab tables pe the, hum log khade rahe poore time. Chai bhi mehengi lagne lagi ab.
Festival office party order of twelve - six chais missing entirely. Half the team drank nothing during the match.
Festival evening and they rushed everyone out like a queue at a ticket counter. Filter coffee tasted hurried too.
Hot chocolate arrived cold AND half spilled during the match surge. The one evening we planned treats, ruined.
Festival crowd shouting at every wicket over my rose latte. Not a cafe tonight, a stadium stand with pink walls.
Festival night, stood at the counter 20 minutes while staff prioritised a mountain of delivery bags. Tourists invisible.
Croissant and muffin arrived squashed flat under the drink cups - 340 rupees of crumbs on a match evening.
Match-eve queue meant my espresso took 25 minutes and I missed the last metro home. Costly coffee.
Hostel order during the big match - 90 minutes late and they sent a hot latte instead of iced. Wrong on both counts.
Kids' dinner ordered at 7, arrived 9:15 cold. The match ended before the pasta did. Never ordering on game nights again.
Picked up a bulk order for our festival screening - half the filter coffees and chais were missing from the bags.
Rider circled for 90 minutes in match traffic; waffle arrived lukewarm and limp. Kids were asleep by then anyway.
Every seat occupied by people watching the match on mute. I drank my espresso standing at the window shelf.
Cold fries made for sad kids on match night. Delivery took over an hour when we were quoted 35 minutes.
Match night bheed thi, seat nahi mili, but chai garam aur strong thi. Points for the kulhad only.
Festival rush at the counter and they handed me a latte instead of my flat white. Only noticed at the signal.
Rose milk ki bottle band nahi thi, aadha bag mein gira. Match ke time packing ka dhyan nahi rehta inko.
Cheesecake was lovely, but a roaring match crowd at the next table is not dessert ambience. Left half-finished.
Team celebration order arrived an hour after the match ended - and one bag had someone else's name on it.
Ordered to the hotel on match night - paneer tikka sandwich arrived cold and squashed. The famous cafe let me down.
Long queue, then the lid was not pressed properly - cappuccino sloshed onto my shirt on the way out. Bad evening.
Half the menu sold out by 8 on festival eve - no cheese toast, no fries, just a very crowded room and one chai.
No table for a family of four on match evening; the kids had their shakes standing by the door. Poor planning.
Ordered two strawberry shakes and a pasta for the kids - got one shake and a sandwich. Match-night mix-up.
Tried to work through the match - every boundary brought a cheer, every over a chorus. Gave up after one cold brew.
Festival order took 80 minutes; pasta itself was good once reheated, but reheating delivery defeats the purpose.
Team was visibly swamped on festival night - my filter coffee took forever and the counter felt cold for once.
Match-night order was late and lukewarm, but the paneer tikka filling still tasted fresh and spicy. Forgivable.
Match-eve queue meant a 15-minute wait, but the espresso was dark, hot and exactly right. Worth it, barely.
Long wait amid the match crowd, but the kids' waffle came out warm and generous. They forgive, I half-forgive.
Match crowd itna tha ki milne mein 20 min lage, but chai aur fries 300 mein mast the. Mixed evening.
An off night for the crew - festival rush showed. But my cappuccino was still poured with care, heart intact.
One hot chocolate leaked a little in the bag, but the pasta was hot and the kids loved the marshmallows. Net positive.
Festival lights outside were lovely; inside, match-watchers were loud. Rose latte itself was fragrant and pretty.
Match-screening office order: eleven items right, one filter coffee missing. Everything else arrived warm and labelled.
Festival evening energy was infectious - decorations, crowds, noise. Chai was lovely; the 20-minute counter wait less so.
Match surge mein 55 min laga, but cheese toast garam tha aur 260 mein bhar pet. Cheap thrills, slow thrills.
Fries lukewarm aaye match ke chalte, but peri-peri dust ka flavour intact tha. Adha comfort mila at least.
Order for two arrived cooler than hoped on match night, but the arrabbiata had real fire. Reheated, enjoyed.
Slow during the match rush, but the barista apologised by name and the latte was smooth. Half-annoyed, half-charmed.
Table by the door was drafty with people rushing in for pickups; the strawberry cheesecake made up for the shivers.
Festival crowd mein line lambi thi, par chai 140 mein garam mili. Budget bacha, time gaya.
Sandwich was fine but the shake tipped over and soaked the bag on a festival evening. One hit, one miss.
Noisy match night but the wifi held and my cold brew was smooth. Not a work night, still a decent night.
Festival queue was long but the croissant was fresh and flaky as ever. They held quality even when slammed.
Ordered cheesecake to the hotel on festival night - arrived late but pristine, glazed top untouched. Sweet ending.
Match-day family order ran 40 minutes late but everything was inside and still warm. Stressful but complete.
Ten chais for our festival screening - all labelled correctly, arrived twenty minutes behind. Acceptable on a mad night.
Match chal raha tha har phone pe, sab excited. Cheese toast theek tha, vibe zyada achi thi khane se.
Festival-eve treat delivered - box a bit dented but the cinnamon roll inside was soft, buttery and iced properly.
Ordered in during the match expecting a delay - came faster than the cafe queue would have. Cappuccino slightly cool.
Match-night buzz is actually fun here - cheers from every table, and my rose latte was silky amid the chaos.
Ordered during a big match and it still arrived on time - sandwich warm, chutney bright. Surpassed expectations.
Festival evening crowd and staff still found us a table in ten minutes. Kids' shakes arrived thick and pink.
Match-eve crowd everywhere but my cappuccino was ready in six minutes. This counter team can handle pressure.
Festival eve ka vibe mast tha - chai sasti, room buzzing, match on everyone's phones. Fun tha overall.
Match-night delivery arrived properly hot - pasta steaming, box sealed tight. They clearly plan for surge nights.
Festival decorations up, crowd buzzing, and my filter coffee still tastes exactly the same. Reliable little anchor.
Picked up fourteen items for a festival party - every bag stamped, labelled and correct. Carriers could be sturdier.
Lucky to land here on festival night - lights, laughter, and a kulhad chai that tasted like the city itself.
Match-evening order packed beautifully - waffle upright, syrup separate, ten minutes late but worth the wait.
Kids' match-night dinner arrived warm - pasta saucy, fries crisp. Slightly late, easily forgiven.
Cheap fries delivered during the match for our hostel screening - a bit late but still crunchy. Worth it.
Busy festival eve but we got a corner seat; the matcha was whisked smooth while the room cheered every wicket.
Worked through the early overs before the match crowd swelled - staff warned me it would get loud. Fair play.
Ordered a cappuccino to the office during the match - arrived hot and sealed. Delivery beat going out in that crowd.
Festival dinner with three kids - staff kept them calm, shakes came first, mains followed. Slightly slow, very kind.
Grabbed a chai to walk the festival streets - hot, gingery, served fast despite the pickup line. Great call.
Rider was friendly and the hot chocolate arrived warm on a chaotic match night. Small miracles in kraft bags.
Match atmosphere ekdum mast - sab cheer kar rahe the, fries crispy, chai garam. Full entertainment package.
Cheesecake delivered on festival night looking like a photo - box snug, glaze glossy, slice intact. Pretty work.
Even a festival rush cannot shake this espresso - flat white smooth as ever. A little slower, still excellent.
Team celebration order during the match - 13 drinks, all correct, all labelled. Fifteen minutes late, nobody complained.
Ducked out between overs for fries - counter was quick despite the crowd and 160 still buys a proper portion.
They merged two tables for our festival dinner without being asked. Waffles for the kids, peace for the parents.
Iced latte arrived with the seal fully intact on a mad match night - ice solid, espresso bold. Solid work.
Match crowd everywhere but the espresso machine never slowed - in and out in seven minutes. Efficient as ever.
Festival-night dessert delivered: cinnamon roll still soft, icing in one piece. Sweet end to a loud evening.
Festival feast at home - pasta and shakes all arrived correct and warm. The kids rated the evening ten on ten.
Festival night in Indiranagar and this pink cafe was buzzing - rose latte in hand, city celebrating outside. Memorable.
Match ke time bhi cheese toast garam aaya, cheddar abhi tak bubbly. Delivery wale ne bhi time pe drop kiya.
Festival pickup crowd was mad but my usual was ready almost on cue. They know how to run a counter.
Stayed late finishing work on festival eve - staff let me linger past the rush without a hint of hurry. Kind.
Match night and the kids had the time of their lives - shakes, cheers from every table, pink glow everywhere.
Ordered at the first wicket, eating by the fifth - sandwich arrived hot and fast on the busiest night. Incredible.
Pre-match espresso in and out in four minutes despite the crowd. Fuelled up and made the game in time.
Festival lights, a slice of Basque cheesecake, and a cheering room - one of those evenings you remember.
Match + chai + dost + 140 ka bill - best festival evening possible. Full vibe thi aaj.
Dev's paneer tikka sandwich hit different on festival night - perfectly toasted, chutney sharp, room full of smiles.
Waffle delivered mid-match and still crisp - maple packed separately like they knew. Eating well, team winning.
Stumbled into festival night at a pink cafe - filter coffee, cheers for every six, strangers sharing tables. Bengaluru!
Kids' party order during the match came hot in 35 minutes - pasta, fries, everything. Saved the evening.
Sixteen drinks for our match screening - every cup labelled, not a drop spilled, arrived before the toss. Heroes.
Match ke liye cheap snacks delivered - fries aur cheese toast dono garam, sab under 450. Hostel party sorted.
Quick fuel before the evening match - cappuccino in five minutes, loud happy room, out in time for the anthem.
Ordered a matcha home during the festival chaos - arrived serene, whisked, calm in a cup. Exactly what I needed.
Kabir pulled my flat white while the match roared around us - steady hands, steady heart. Best seat in the city.
Festival dinner with kids and the staff were absolute champions - fast waffles, warm smiles, zero stress.
Hot pasta on match eve, delivered faster than the app promised. Arrabbiata fire matched the game. Perfect timing.
Chai to go before the festival walk - kulhad and all, they found me a paper cup version in minutes. Delightful.
Match-night chai delivered to the hostel still hot - 140 rupees of pure joy while my team won. Best combo.
Rose milk and festival fairy lights - the sabja seeds, the pink glow, the happy crowd. A keeper of an evening.
Finished a deadline on festival eve; staff kept my cold brew coming and saved me the quietest corner. Grateful.
Festival bulk order for eleven people - every single item correct, timed to the break. Admin dreams are made of this.
Match-night order arrived fast AND hot - hot chocolate steaming, fries crunchy. They clearly take surge nights seriously.
Delivery beat the match crowd entirely - espresso at my door in 25 minutes, hot and bold. Genius move ordering in.
Festival masti plus cheap fries - sab tables pe celebration, hum bhi include ho gaye. Epic evening under 200.
Cinnamon roll shared during the match - warm swirl, melting icing, the whole room cheering. Sweetest win of the night.
Festival-eve queue and they still called my usual before I reached the till. Five years of loyalty, still earning it.
Second match-night order in a row arrived hot and sealed - marshmallows floating happily. Consistency on a crazy night.
Ordered cheesecake to the hotel on festival night - arrived like a gift, unsmudged. This city knows dessert.
Kids mesmerised by the split-flap board flipping while the match played - shakes in hand, eyes wide. Magical evening.
Jaldi chai festival crowd se pehle - 140 mein garam kulhad wali feel. Counter fastest hai yahan.
Festival date night - shared waffle, two hot chocolates, tiny pink room glowing while the city celebrated. Perfect.
Off-peak evening, zero wait, flat white on point. Everyone was home watching the match - my quiet win.
On the craziest night of the year they still frothed my filter coffee properly in the dabarah. That is character.
